groups.passage:
Aesop, the Greek writer of fables, was sitting by the roadside one day when a traveler asked him what sort of people lived in Athens. Aesop replied, “Tell me where you come from and what sort of people live there, and I’ll tell you what sort of people you’ll find in Athens.” [[16]], the man answered, “I come from Argos, and there the people are all friendly, generous, and warm-hearted. I love them.” [[17]] this, Aesop answered, “I’m happy to tell you, my dear friend, that you’ll find the people of Athens much the same.”
A few hours later, [[18]] traveler came down the road. He too stopped and asked Aesop the same question. [[19]], Aesop made the same request. But frowning, the man answered, “I’m from Argos and there the people are unfriendly, [[20]], and vicious. They’re thieves and murderers, all of them.” “Well, I’m afraid you’ll find the people of Athens much the same,” replied Aesop.

Not only will the summit lose its tourist attraction, but the disappearance of the snows will also cause major damage to the ecosystem on the dry African plains at its base. [[24]] the snow covering the peak, there will not be enough moisture and water to nourish the plants and animals below. groups.passage: Most human beings actually decide before they think. When people encounter a complex issue and form an opinion, how thoroughly have they [[26]] all the important factors involved before they make their decisions? The answer is: not very thoroughly, [[27]] they are executives, specialized experts, or ordinary people in the street. Very few people, no matter how intelligent or experienced, can [[28]] all the possibilities or outcomes of a policy or a course of action within just a short period of time. Those who take pride in being decisive often try their best to consider all the factors beforehand. [[29]], it is not unusual for them to come up with a decision before they have the time to do so. And [[30]] an opinion is formed, most of their thinking then is simply trying to find support for it.

groups.passage:
In English-speaking cultures, the choice of first names for children can be prompted by many factors: tradition, religion, nature, culture, and fashion, to name just a few.
Certain people like to give a name that has been handed down in the family to show [[31]] for or to remember a relative whom they love or admire. Some families have a tradition of [[32]] the father’s first name to the first born son. In other families, a surname is included in the selection of a child’s given name to [[33]] a family surname going. It may be the mother’s maiden name, for instance.
For a long time, [[34]] has also played an important role in naming children. Boys’ names such as John, Peter, and Thomas are chosen from the Bible. Girls’ names such as Faith, Patience, and Sophie (wisdom) are chosen because they symbolize Christian qualities. However, for people who are not necessarily religious but are fond of nature, names [[35]] things of beauty are often favored. Flower and plant names like Heather, Rosemary, and Iris [[36]] this category.
Another factor that has had a great [[37]] on the choice of names is the spread of culture through the media. People may choose a name because they are strongly [[38]] a character in a book or a television series; they may also adopt names of famous people or their favorite actors and actresses. Sometimes, people pick foreign names for their children because those names are unusual and will thus make their children more [[39]] and distinctive.
Finally, some people just pick a name the sound of which they like, [[40]] of its meaning, its origins, or its popularity. However, even these people may look at the calendar to pick a lucky day when they make their choice.

tags.topic: factors in choosing children’s first names in English-speaking cultures

groups.passage:
American writer Toni Morrison was born in 1931 in Ohio. She was raised in an African American family filled with songs and stories of Southern myths, which later shaped her prose. Her happy family life led to her excellent performance in school, despite the atmosphere of racial discrimination in the society.
After graduating from college, Morrison started to work as a teacher and got married in 1958. Several years later, her marriage began to fail. For a temporary escape, she joined a small writers’ group, in which each member was required to bring a story or poem for discussion. She wrote a story based on the life of a girl she knew in childhood who had prayed to God for blue eyes. The story was well received by the group, but then she put it away, thinking she was done with it.
In 1964, Morrison got divorced and devoted herself to writing. One day, she dusted off the story she had written for the writers’ group and decided to make it into a novel. She drew on her memories from childhood and expanded upon them using her imagination so that the characters developed a life of their own. The Bluest Eye was eventually published in 1970. From 1970 to 1992, Morrison published five more novels.
In her novels, Morrison brings in different elements of the African American past, their struggles, problems and cultural memory. In Song of Solomon, for example, Morrison tells the story of an African American man and his search for identity in his culture. The novels and other works won her several prizes. In 1993, Morrison received the Nobel Prize in Literature. She is the eighth woman and the first African American woman to win the honor.

groups.passage:
Below is an excerpt from an interview with Zeke Emanuel, a health-policy expert, on his famous brothers.
Interviewer: You’re the older brother of Rahm, the mayor of Chicago, and Ari, an extremely successful talent agent. And you’re a bioethicist and one of the architects of Obamacare. Isn’t writing a book about how great your family is a bit odd?
Zeke: I don’t write a book about how great my family is. There are lots of idiocies and foolishness—a lot to make fun of in the book. I wrote Brothers Emanuel because I had begun jotting stories for my kids. And then we began getting a lot of questions: What did Mom put in the cereal? Three successful brothers, all different areas.
I: To what do you attribute the Emanuel brothers’ success?
Z: I would put success in quotes. We strive. First, I think we got this striving from our mother to make the world a better place. A second important thing is you never rest on the last victory. There’s always more to do. And maybe the third important thing is my father’s admonition that offense is the best defense. We don’t give up.
I: Do you still not have a TV?
Z: I don’t own a TV. I don’t own a car. I don’t Facebook. I don’t tweet.
I: But you have four cell phones.
Z: I’m down to two, thankfully.
I: Your brothers are a national source of fascination. Where do you think they’ll be in five years?
Z: Ari will be a superagent running the same company. Rahm would still be mayor of Chicago. I will probably continue to be my academic self. The one thing I can guarantee is none of us will have taken a cruise, none of us will be sitting on a beach with a pina colada.

options.A: The secret to bringing up successful kids.
options.B: The recipe for a breakfast food.

groups.passage:
MOOC, a massive open online course, aims at providing large-scale interactive participation and open access via the web. In addition to traditional course materials such as videos, readings, and problem sets, MOOCs provide interactive user forums that help build a community for the students, professors, and teaching assistants.
MOOCs first made waves in the fall of 2011, when Professor Sebastian Thrun from Stanford University opened his graduate-level artificial intelligence course up to any student anywhere, and 160,000 students in more than 190 countries signed up. This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways. Since the courses can be taken by hundreds of thousands of students at the same time, the number of universities might decrease dramatically. Professor Thrun has even envisioned a future in which there will only need to be 10 universities in the world. Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free. This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.
There is a lot of excitement and fear surrounding MOOCs. While some say free online courses are a great way to increase the enrollment of minority students, others have said they will leave many students behind. Some critics have said that MOOCs promote an unrealistic one-size-fits-all model of higher education and that there is no replacement for true dialogues between professors and their students. After all, a brain is not a computer. We are not blank hard drives waiting to be filled with data. People learn from people they love and remember the things that arouse emotion. Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.

options.B: Many courses are offered by famous universities.
options.D: Many students can take the course at the same time.

options.D: The lack of social interaction among students and professors.

tags.topic: MOOCs (massive open online courses) and their impact on higher education

groups.passage:
Today the car seems to make periodic leaps in progress. A variety of driver assistance technologies are appearing on new cars. A developing technology called Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication, or V2V, is being tested by automotive manufacturers as a way to help reduce the number of accidents. V2V works by using wireless signals to send information back and forth between cars about their location, speed and direction, so that they keep safe distances from each other. Another new technology being tested is Vehicle-to-Infrastructure communication, or V2I. V2I would allow vehicles to communicate with road signs or traffic signals and provide information to the vehicle about safety issues. V2I could also request traffic information from a traffic management system and access the best possible routes. Both V2V and V2I have the potential to reduce around 80 percent of vehicle crashes on the road.
More and more new cars can reverse-park, read traffic signs, maintain a safe distance in steady traffic and brake automatically to avoid crashes. Moreover, a number of firms are creating cars that drive themselves to a chosen destination without a human at the controls. It is predicted that driverless cars will be ready for sale within five years. If and when cars go completely driverless, the benefits will be enormous. Google, which already uses prototypes of such cars to ferry its staff along Californian freeways, once put a blind man in a prototype and filmed him being driven off to buy takeaway hamburgers. If this works, huge numbers of elderly and disabled people can regain their personal mobility. The young will not have to pay crippling motor insurance, because their reckless hands and feet will no longer touch the wheel or the accelerator. People who commute by car will gain hours each day to work, rest, or read a newspaper.

options.C: V2V is designed to decrease crashes by keeping safe distances.
options.D: Through V2V, a car can warn cyclists nearby of its approach.

options.C: People can race cars to their heart’s content.
options.D: A blind man can get into a car and travel safely.

options.C: Everyone, including children, can afford a car.
options.D: The production of driverless cars is still far away.

tags.topic: vehicle communication technologies (V2V, V2I) and the benefits of driverless cars

questions.label: 中譯英1
questions.stem: 有些年輕人辭掉都市裡的高薪工作，返回家鄉種植有機蔬菜。
questions.scoring_notes:
第一大題是「中譯英」，題型與過去幾年相同，考生需將兩個中文句子譯成正確、通順、達意的英文，兩題合計為 8 分。
評分標準與歷年相同，在「中譯英」部分，每小題總分 4 分，原則上是每個錯誤扣 0.5 分。
今年的「中譯英」與「年輕人返鄉種植有機蔬菜」的趨勢有關，評量的重點在於考生能否能運用常用的詞彙與基本句型將兩句中文翻譯成正確達意的英文句子，所測驗之句型為高中生熟悉的範圍，詞彙亦控制在大考中心詞彙表四級內之詞彙，中等程度以上的考生，如果能使用正確句型並注意用字、拼字，應能得理想的分數。例如：「辭掉都市裡的高薪工作」若譯成(have) quit high-paying/well-paid job/jobs in the city 即可得分；「藉由決心與努力」則可翻譯為 through/with/because of determination and effort/efforts。在選取樣卷時，我們發現有不少考生對於英文詞彙的使用及英文拼字仍有加強的空間，如第一句的「返回家鄉」有考生翻譯為 backed to home，「成功了」有不少考生翻譯為 success 或 successed；在拼字方面，「更健康」healthier 有考生少寫了字母 “i”，「蔬菜」vegetables 這個字拼錯的考生也不少，相當可惜。

patterns: and 連接兩個動作（辭掉…，返回…）
to + V 表目的（返回家鄉種植…）

figures.label: 四格連環圖片
figures.description: 黑白手繪四格漫畫（人物的書包背帶塗成淡綠色），排成2×2方格，中央小圓圈標示閱讀順序「1 2／3 4」（左上1、右上2、左下3、右下4）。圖1（左上）：兩名穿制服、斜背書包的學生並肩走在彎曲的道路上。左邊綁馬尾的女生低著頭，雙手拿著手機專心看螢幕；右邊的男生戴著大耳罩式耳機，閉著眼睛、面帶笑容，一手高舉隨身音樂播放器，邊走邊陶醉在音樂裡（頭上畫著音符）。遠處路上有一位媽媽牽著小孩走路。圖2（右上）：女生一頭撞上路邊的大樹（樹幹旁畫著表示撞擊的鋸齒狀爆炸線），閉眼、張嘴露出痛苦表情，手機從手中掉落；男生仍戴著耳機、閉著眼睛微笑，舉著音樂播放器繼續往前走（頭上畫著音符），完全沒注意到；遠處牽著小孩的媽媽用手摀著嘴，一臉驚訝。圖3（左下）：戴耳機的男生閉著眼睛、面帶笑容，揮著手走到一輛車子前方；車上的駕駛皺眉、咬牙，一臉怒氣（頭旁畫著冒氣的符號），正猛按喇叭（畫著喇叭與表示巨響的鋸齒狀爆炸線），車牌號碼為「8888」。圖4（右下）：空白，只畫了一個大問號「?」，由考生想像故事的後續發展與結局。圖中除了車牌「8888」與格子編號外沒有其他文字。

questions.label: 作文
questions.stem: 提示︰請仔細觀察以下三幅連環圖片的內容，並想像第四幅圖片可能的發展，寫一篇涵蓋所有連環圖片內容且有完整結局的故事。
questions.scoring_notes:
「英文作文」的評分標準是依據內容、組織、文法句構、詞彙拼字、體例五個項目給分，字數明顯不足的作文則扣總分 1 分。
第二大題是「英文作文」，考生須從三幅連環圖片的內容，想像第四幅圖片可能的發展，再以至少 120 個單詞寫出一個涵蓋連環圖片內容並有完整結局的故事。
今年的「英文作文」主題與考生日常生活經驗相關，重點在於說明青少年若過度使用 3C 電子產品，甚至在走路時還像圖片二裡的女生忙著滑手機或像圖片三裡的男生沉迷於耳機裡的音樂中，將會造成意外，嚴重時還可能危及性命。大部分的考生應能從不同的角度發揮想像力，寫出一個涵蓋連環圖片內容並有完整結局的故事。評分的考量重點為作文內容是否切題，組織是否具連貫性、句子結構及用字是否適切、以及拼字與標點符號的使用是否正確得當。

tags.topic: accidents caused by using a phone or listening to music while walking (story with an imagined ending)
distracted walking with phones and earphones (overuse of 3C devices)

extraction.method: 題本文字以 Word 版 paper-2.docx 為主（以 lxml 走訪 document.xml 的全部 w:r，底線 run 內的數字轉成 [[題號]]，只有底線空白的 run 轉成 _____），再以程式將全部 282 個文字欄位（大題與部分標題、說明、題組標示、選文各段、題幹、選項、選項庫）與 pdftotext -layout（paper-1.pdf，NFC 正規化後）逐段比對（英文比對連續詞序列、中文去空白後比對子字串），除空格與其後標點之間的排版空白外全部一致；Read 看 PDF 全部 8 頁頁面影像確認段落切分、首行縮排、粗體／斜體／底線與方框，英文作文的四格漫畫另以 pdftoppm -r 250 放大裁切逐格判讀；答案取自 answer.pdf（pdftotext -layout）；評分原則取自 scoring.pdf（pdftotext 與 -layout，並以 Read 看頁面影像核對）逐字摘錄；統計以 xlrd 讀 stats-1.xls（英文工作表：答對率 P、高分組 Ph、低分組 Pl、鑑別度 D）、stats-2.xls（英文工作表：選項分析 T／H／L 列、未答）、stats-3.xls（英文科非選擇題分數人數統計表），並以程式交叉核對（選項分析 T 列標 * 的選項＝官方答案，56 題全部；T／H／L 列正答比例＝P／Ph／Pl，56 題全部；D＝Ph−Pl，56 題全部；非選擇題兩題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數 145,575）。
issues: 結構核對：與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 期別「94–110」一致——詞彙題 1–15（15分）、綜合測驗 16–30（3篇×5題，題組標示16–20、21–25、26–30，15分）、文意選填 31–40（A–J，10分）、閱讀測驗 41–56（4篇×4題，每題2分，32分）、中譯英 2題×4分、英文作文 20分（文長至少120個單詞，與 essay_length_by_year「101-110」相符）；第壹部分單選題 72分＋第貳部分非選擇題 28分＝100分；封面「考試時間：100 分鐘」「單選題共 56 題」「非選擇題共二大題」。無差異。
validator warning「題號重複 [1, 2]」為預期：中譯英兩題題本編為 1.、2.，英文作文沒有題號（no 填 1）；no 必須是整數，故沿用題本編號（與 gsat-104／106 相同做法），並以 label「中譯英1」「中譯英2」「作文」區分，label 無重複。

中譯英：評分原則沒有公布完整參考譯文，只舉出片段譯法（「辭掉都市裡的高薪工作」若譯成 (have) quit high-paying/well-paid job/jobs in the city 即可得分；「藉由決心與努力」可譯為 through/with/because of determination and effort/efforts）與常見錯誤（backed to home、success／successed、healthier 少寫 i、vegetables 拼錯）；這些不是整句譯文，故 answer 與 accepted_answers 皆為 null，片段譯法保留在 scoring_notes 原文中。評分原則的中譯英段落同時談兩句，無法逐句切開而不破壞原文，故兩題的 scoring_notes 都放：第一段「第一大題是「中譯英」…兩題合計為 8 分。」、評分標準句「評分標準與歷年相同…原則上是每個錯誤扣 0.5 分。」（本年沒有「相同的錯誤只扣一次」一句）、整段中譯英說明（逐字），以換行分隔。評分原則原文「考生能否能運用常用的詞彙」多一個「能」，依逐字原則保留。

英文作文：評分原則沒有官方範文，answer 為 null；題目沒有規定段數，tags 不填 paragraphs（與 gsat-106 同為看圖寫作，essay_type 標 picture）。scoring_notes 由評分原則三處逐字摘錄組成（「英文作文」評分標準句、第一段中「第二大題是「英文作文」，考生須從三幅連環圖片…完整結局的故事。」、最後一段作文說明），以換行分隔。本年評分項目為五項（內容、組織、文法句構、詞彙拼字、體例），與 spec 所記 106 年起才改為四項一致。

英文作文圖（s6g1 figures）：Word 版只有一張圖片、PDF 文字層沒有圖中文字，四格內容依 250dpi 頁面影像逐格描述（圖中唯一文字為車牌「8888」與中央的格子編號 1–4）。圖1 女生手上的裝置依評分原則「圖片二裡的女生忙著滑手機」寫作手機，男生手上的是隨身音樂播放器（頭戴耳罩式耳機、頭上有音符），評分原則稱「圖片三裡的男生沉迷於耳機裡的音樂中」。圖2 女生撞到樹、手機掉落；圖3 駕駛對走在車前的男生猛按喇叭——此為依影像的描述，不是官方文字。

段落切分：Word 版第16–20題選文「…I love them.”」與「[[17]] this, Aesop answered…」、第21–25題選文「…will soon」與「[[22]]. According to…」、第31–40題選文「…a child’s given name to」與「[[33]] a family surname going.」被拆成不同段落，但後一段沒有首行縮排（其他段落都有 firstLine 縮排），PDF 頁面影像上也是同一段落的換行（為了讓空格落在行首而強制斷行），故以一個空白接回同一段。選文段數：16–20 兩段、21–25 一段、26–30 一段、31–40 五段、41–44 四段、49–52 三段、53–56 兩段。

第45–48題選文：題本先以一行「Below is an excerpt from an interview with Zeke Emanuel, a health-policy expert, on his famous brothers.」（方框外）引出，訪談內容印在方框內，說話者首次標「Interviewer:」「Zeke:」，之後縮寫為「I:」「Z:」。passage 第一行放這句引言，其後每個說話輪次各一行，說話者標示照題本原文。
第11、12題題本的空格是一段加底線的空白（Word 版為 5 個加底線空格，PDF 影像上是一條短底線，沒有底線字元），統一寫成「_____」（5 個底線）；其他詞彙題題幹的底線長度照題本原樣保留（5–8 個 _）。
題組標示：Word 版寫「第16至20 題為題組」、pdftotext 為「第 16 至 20 題為題組」（中英混排字距），group_label 統一寫成「第16至20題為題組」（與 gsat-104 等檔一致）。

格式：題本中 The Snows of Kilimanjaro（21–25 選文）、The Bluest Eye（41–44 選文與第42題 (A)）、Song of Solomon、Brothers Emanuel（45–48 選文）為斜體；cash-strapped（49–52 選文與第49題）、第50與55題的 NOT、第54題的 infrastructure 為粗體；題組標示有底線；45–48 訪談在方框內。依 schema 不保留粗斜體（題目以引號指稱，非「畫底線的字」，故未加 <u>）。

逐字保留的原文寫法：第21–25題選文「Earnest Hemingway’s」（作家名常拼作 Ernest）；第45–48題選文「pina colada」（無 ñ）與「I don’t write a book about how great my family is」（現在式）；第44題 (C)「What she wrote in her novels are true stories of African Americans.」（主詞子句配 are）；第31–40題選文「the first born son」。皆照題本，未更正。

文字來源細節：PDF 選項庫印作「( I ) respect」「( J ) unique」（括號內有空白），代號統一為 I／J。第16、19、20、22、29題等空格後的標點依題本緊接空格（例「[[16]], the man answered」「soon [[22]]. According」），PDF 版面在空格與標點間的空白不保留。pdftotext 的題本文字層有 CJK 相容表意字（例「連」U+F99A），JSON 以 Word 版文字為準，已確認整份 JSON 為 NFC 正規形式、無相容表意字。

評分原則 PDF：文字層把第一句提到的字母寫成「“i ”」（右引號前多一個空白），頁面影像上是「“i”」，已依影像改為「“i”」。跨行接合時，一側是英文字母或數字的位置補一個空白（例「扣 / 0.5 分」→「扣 0.5 分」、「success 或 / successed」→「success 或 successed」），中文與中文、全形標點處直接接合；「vegetables 這個字」的空白為文字層原有。

選擇題統計：stats-2.xls 只有 T 列以 * 標示正答（H、L 列沒有 *），已核對 T 列 * 選項＝官方答案（56 題全部），且 T／H／L 列正答比例與 stats-1.xls 的 P／Ph／Pl 完全相同（本年沒有四捨五入差異），stats-1 的 D＝Ph−Pl 全部 56 題成立。各題 option_rates（加未答）因四捨五入加總為 0.99–1.01；option_rates_high／option_rates_low 加總 0.98–1.01（第56題 L 列加總 0.98，另有未答 2%）。omit_rate 為全體（T 列）未答比例，只有第45、56題為 1%，其餘 0；H／L 列的未答（第53–55題 L 列 1%、第56題 L 列 2%）未收錄。stats-1.xls 的五組通過率 Pa–Pe 與 D1–D4 未收錄。

低答對率／低或負鑑別度題目已複核非對齊錯誤（皆為大考中心原始數據，T 列 * 選項＝官方答案）：第15題 P=0.23、D=−0.03（40% 選 A departed，高分組 51% 選 A）；第17題 P=0.17、D=−0.20（39% 選 B By、41% 選 C For，高分組 B／C 各 46%，正答 A At 只有 8%）；第29題 P=0.63、D=0.15（低分組也有 53% 答對）；第41題 D=0.31（P=0.89，高分組 100%）；第45題 P=0.42、D=0.31（36% 選 C）；第35題 P=0.35（18% 選 A drawn to）；第26、27、38題 P=0.40。

非選擇題統計：stats-3.xls 只有「第一題（中譯英，滿分8分，兩小題合計）」與「第二題（英文作文，滿分20分）」的分數人數分布，無法拆到中譯英各小題，因此放在 sections[s5].stats 與 sections[s6].stats 的 score_distribution（schema 未定義此欄位，沿用 gsat-104／106 的做法）；rate 為原表百分比÷100，分母是報名人數 147,478（含缺考 1,903；到考 145,575），已核對兩題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數 145,575。原表分數區間「9.00- 9.99」等的空白已去除；第一題 9 分以上的列在原表為空白，未收錄。小題層級 stats 為 null。

標註判斷：第16題 Smiling 與第二位旅人的「But frowning」對照，標 discourse（answer_pos 標 verb，分詞）；第17題「At this」＝聽到這話時，標 phrase／preposition；第18題 another 標 grammar／determiner，answer_pos 允許值沒有限定詞，故省略；第24題「Without the snow…, there will not be…」需由上下文因果判斷，標 discourse；第34題由下文 Bible、Christian、religious 推得 religion，標 discourse；第46題（What does … think of…）依 repo 慣例標 tone_attitude；第48題（best summarizes … response）需綜合三兄弟的回答推得「不會有什麼改變」，標 inference；第54題問 infrastructure 在文中所指，標 vocab_in_context。s4g2 為雜誌訪談逐字稿，genre 標 dialogue。sdgs：21–25 冰河融化標 [13, 15]；49–52 MOOCs 標 [4]；53–56 車聯網減少車禍與自駕車標 [3, 9, 11]；作文（分心走路的交通安全）標 [3]；其餘無明顯相關，填空陣列或不填。

本檔新增的非 schema 欄位：section.part_title／part_instructions（第壹、貳部分標題與第貳部分共同說明，放在該部分的第一個大題 s1、s5）、section.stats（非選擇題分數分布）、group.group_label（「第16至20題為題組」等題本原文）、figure.label、sources.paper_word、question.stats.option_rates_high／option_rates_low／omit_rate。
